name: P'yanitsa (Russian Drunkard)
description: P'yanitsa (The Drunkard) is the most popular children's card game in Russia, acting as the Eastern European equivalent to the western game of 'War'. It is a game of pure chance and endurance where players aim to capture the entire deck. Its unique characteristic is the '6 beats Ace' rule, which prevents the highest card from being invincible. It is exceptionally simple, making it a staple of Russian childhood and social gatherings.

history.origins: Dates back to the 19th century in the Russian Empire. It was originally played with the standard 36-card deck used for Durak and other traditional Russian games.
timeline: 1850s: First documented rules in Russian game manuals.
1917: Survives the revolution as a popular 'proletariat' game due to its simplicity.
1960s: Standardized children's version ('Drunkard') becomes a household name in the USSR.
Present: Still the first game taught to most Russian children.
history.cultural: The name 'P'yanitsa' (Drunkard) comes from the way the cards 'toss and turn' without player control, much like a person in an intoxicated state.
history.evolution: The '6 beats Ace' rule was likely added to simulate folk stories of the 'little guy' overcoming the powerful.

setup.players: 2 is standard; up to 4 is possible.
setup.dealing: The entire deck is dealt face-down to all players. Players do not look at their cards.

rules.objective: Capture the entire deck by winning tricks: each round players reveal the top card simultaneously; the higher rank takes the trick (six beats ace). The player who collects all the cards wins; the opponent left with no cards is the loser, the drunkard.
rules.gameplay: 1. Each player turns over their top card simultaneously. 2. The highest card wins all cards in the trick. 3. Winning cards are placed at the bottom of the winner's deck. 4. Exception: An Ace is the highest card, UNLESS a 6 is played against it. A 6 beats an Ace (but loses to every other card).
keyRules: 6 beats Ace (but loses to all other cards).
Disputes: same rank playedâ€”each adds one face-down, one face-up; highest face-up wins pile.

strategy.basic: As a game of 100% chance, there is no active strategy. However, the '6 beats Ace' mechanic means that your deck's health is cyclical. If you have many 6s, you are effectively protected against an opponent with many Aces.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Bottom-Loading' Effect: In physical play, the order in which you pick up the tricks and place them at the bottom of your deck matters. Savvy players try to sandwich high cards between lower cards to avoid 'Dispute' clusters later in the game.
strategy.advanced: Stamina Tracking: In long games, players begin to memorize the 'Loop' of their cards. If you know a cluster of Jacks is coming up, you can predict when you might enter a Dispute round.
tips: Play with the 'Giveaway' variant if the game lasts too longâ€”whoever loses all their cards first wins.
Be careful during Disputes; losing a high-stakes Dispute can flip the entire game balance in seconds.
